plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the U-Net architecture used as the noise-prediction backbone in a diffusion model. The diagram is organized as a symmetric encoder-decoder structure: the encoder path (left branch) shows a sequence of orange-shaded three-dimensional feature map volumes that progressively downsample the input from 256×256×3 through 256×256×128, 128×128×128, 64×64×256, 32×32×256, 16×16×512, down to 8×8×512 at the bottleneck, while the decoder path (right branch) shows dark steel-blue feature map volumes that mirror the encoder at each spatial scale as the resolution is progressively restored. The sizes of these volumes correspond to the input sizes; for example, the block for 256x256x3 has a large shape thins hape while 8x8x512 is long with a small surface. Four horizontal “Concatenate” arrows connect matching encoder and decoder blocks at four resolution levels, forming the characteristic skip connections of a U-Net. A small blue square node labeled “t” injects the diffusion timestep via a “time embedding” branch, with arrows feeding it into each processing block. Two block types are annotated in a legend at lower right: a plain “Res. block” (used at larger spatial scales) and a “Res. block + self-attention” (used at smaller spatial scales near the bottleneck). This figure demonstrates how a conditioned U-Net with residual blocks, skip connections, and time-step injection serves as the learned denoiser in a diffusion generative model.

interactions.label: Encoder-decoder pass
interactions.teaches: The U-Net first compresses spatial resolution while increasing channel capacity, then reconstructs resolution while reusing matching encoder features through skip-connection concatenation

interactions.label: Diffusion timestep t
interactions.teaches: The same timestep condition is embedded once and injected into every residual block, so the denoiser changes its computation depending on the noise level being removed

At the 16×16 resolution, self-attention lets one spatial position mix information from all other positions, unlike a plain residual block whose update is primarily local or channelwise at each position

demo_steps.title: Noisy input enters the U-Net
demo_steps.narration: The left speckled 256×256×3 image is the noisy diffusion sample. The time embedding trunk is already present below the network and will condition every residual block.

demo_steps.title: Encoder downsamples
demo_steps.narration: The highlight moves down the left branch from 256×256 to 16×16. Each step reduces spatial size while increasing or preserving channel capacity, producing compact high-level features.

demo_steps.title: Bottleneck at 8×8
demo_steps.narration: At the bottom, the representation is spatially tiny but channel-rich. This bottleneck carries global structure before the decoder starts rebuilding resolution.

demo_steps.title: Decoder uses skip concatenations
demo_steps.narration: As the highlight moves up the right branch, matching skip arrows pulse when reached. Concatenation restores fine encoder details that would otherwise be lost during downsampling.

demo_steps.title: Timestep changes the denoising behavior
demo_steps.narration: Moving t changes the numeric embedding shown on every blue injection arrow. The architecture stays the same, but each residual block receives a different noise-level condition.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a flat oblique U-Net layout matching the source: x runs left-to-right along the network, y is vertical height, and z/depth is a shallow oblique extrusion up-right. Overall network spans about x=-8 to +8, y=0 to 4.8. Baseline for feature blocks is y=0.8. Feature volume visual height is tied to spatial resolution: 256→3.6 units, 128→1.8, 64→0.9, 32→0.48, 16→0.28, 8→0.18. Feature volume horizontal length is tied to channels: 3→0.12 units for image plates, 128→0.55, 256→0.75, 512→1.25. Use shallow oblique thickness z≈0.22 for all orange feature volumes, with top/right faces visible. Approximate x positions: input plate at -7.3; encoder 256 blocks at -6.6 and -5.9; encoder 128 at -5.2; encoder 64 at -4.35; encoder 32 at -3.25; encoder 16 at -2.05; encoder 8 at -0.65; central bottleneck 8 at 0.8; decoder 16 at 2.05; decoder 32 at 3.1; decoder 64 at 4.0; decoder 128 at 4.75; decoder 256 blocks at 5.45 and 6.15; output plate at 7.25. Blocks sit upright with vertical front faces; top and right edges recede diagonally up-right in the oblique projection. Dominant colors: orange block front #c97956, darker side face #7a3b22, black outlines #111111, skip-connection arrows and Concatenate labels #d07a5b, time embedding trunk and injection arrows blue-gray #486a7a, pale attention legend arrow #8fb1c4, main labels dark brown #7a3b22. Image plates should be thin slabs with procedural gray/noisy texture and small colored speckles. Skip polylines route above the U shape: 256 line near y=4.55 from x≈-5.9 to x≈6.1; 128 line near y=3.25 from x≈-5.0 to x≈5.0; 64 line near y=2.45 from x≈-4.25 to x≈4.1; 32 line near y=2.05 from x≈-3.15 to x≈3.2; optional inner 16 line near y=1.75 from x≈-2.0 to x≈2.1. Place arrowheads at the decoder end of skip connections. Time embedding trunk runs from the t circle at x=-8.0,y=0.25 to x=6.6,y=0.25, with diagonal arrows up-right into each block base.
interactionPlan.notes: Render volumes as extruded boxes with black edge outlines and simple Lambert materials; keep the camera effectively orthographic/oblique so the diagram reads like the textbook figure rather than a free 3D scene. The passState control should animate a bright outline or glow along the active volume, fade previous volumes, and pulse the relevant skip-connection arrow exactly when entering the matching decoder state. The timeStep slider should update small numeric badges on each blue injection arrow, e.g. embed(t)=sinusoidal/MLP(t), without needing to expose the full embedding vector; use a compact displayed scalar or color gradient derived from t. The attention click target should be the 16×16 self-attention block and the legend entry; clicking opens a semi-transparent overlay near the block rather than replacing the whole architecture. In the overlay, draw a 16×16 grid with one query cell highlighted and attention rays or a heatmap to all cells; next to it show a plain residual-block mini-panel with no all-to-all rays. Use sprite or SDF text for labels so rotated dimension labels remain legible.

discrepancies: The input and output noisy image plates appear as very narrow vertical strips rather than broad speckled image panels like the source.
Most network blocks are faded/translucent in the default state and an extra yellow active highlight is shown, whereas the source uses uniformly solid orange/brown blocks.
Extra e(t)=... badges under every block and attention/comparison explanatory text are not present in the source and clutter the diagram.
Several dimension labels are crowded, partly obscured by the legend or other labels, and do not match the cleaner placement and hierarchy of the source.
The lower time-embedding arrows and baseline are visually less clean and more cluttered than the source due to added badges and highlighting.
The overall U-Net is more compressed horizontally and vertically than the source, making the skip concatenation arrows and block proportions less faithful.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure captures the general conditioned U-Net structure with skips and time embedding, but important visual proportions, colors, image plates, and label cleanliness differ noticeably from the source.
action_items: Make the left and right noisy image plates broad textured panels matching the source instead of thin vertical strips.
Use solid orange/brown block colors by default and remove or greatly reduce the active-state fading/highlight when matching the static source.
Remove the e(t) badges and attention explanatory overlay from the default view, or hide them unless explicitly toggled.
Reposition and resize the dimension labels so they are legible, diagonal, and not obscured by the legend or blocks.

feedback.rationale: The core U-Net concept and interactivity are correct, but the issues are implementation-level visual fixes such as panel scale, colors, clutter removal, and label placement.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the U-Net architecture used as the noise-prediction backbone in a diffusion model. The diagram is organized as a symmetric encoder-decoder structure: the encoder path (left branch) shows a sequence of orange-shaded three-dimensional feature map volumes that progressively downsample the input from 256×256×3 through 256×256×128, 128×128×128, 64×64×256, 32×32×256, 16×16×512, down to 8×8×512 at the bottleneck, while the decoder path (right branch) shows dark steel-blue feature map volumes that mirror the encoder at each spatial scale as the resolution is progressively restored. The sizes of these volumes correspond to the input sizes; for example, the block for 256x256x3 has a large shape thins hape while 8x8x512 is long with a small surface. Four horizontal “Concatenate” arrows connect matching encoder and decoder blocks at four resolution levels, forming the characteristic skip connections of a U-Net. A small blue square node labeled “t” injects the diffusion timestep via a “time embedding” branch, with arrows feeding it into each processing block. Two block types are annotated in a legend at lower right: a plain “Res. block” (used at larger spatial scales) and a “Res. block + self-attention” (used at smaller spatial scales near the bottleneck). This figure demonstrates how a conditioned U-Net with residual blocks, skip connections, and time-step injection serves as the learned denoiser in a diffusion generative model.
